planets.name: 51 Peg b
planets.description: Planet of 51 Peg found by radial velocity, with a 4.23-day year, found in 1995.

radius.source: the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since 51 Peg b does not transit

mass.source: Cont et al. (2026), A&A 710, A345, Table 1: 0.61 (+0.06, -0.05) Jupiter masses, from the Doppler shift of the planet's own spectral lines

orbit.source: Cont et al. (2026), A&A 710, A345, Tables 1 and 2 (tilt 49.8 +5.8/-5.7 degrees from the planet's own Doppler shift; eccentricity fixed to zero, 2-sigma limit 0.0063; a/R* is its 0.052 au over the star's recorded 847,269 km)

text.card: 51 Peg b was found in 1995 by radial velocity; it does not cross its star.
text.introduction: It is the only planet known around 51 Peg. Its orbit, tilt included, follows Cont et al. 2026's fit, and its size is the archive's model from its mass.
text.locator: Cont et al. (2026), A&A 710, A345, Tables 1 and 2: P_orb 4.2307966 d, T_C 2456326.9323 BJD_TDB, i 49.8 deg, M_p 0.61 M_Jup, a 0.052 au; NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CONT_ET_AL_2026): disc_year 1995, disc_facility Haute-Provence Observatory, sy_pnum 1; pscomppars calculated pl_radj 1.26

quotes.title: 51 Pegasi b
quotes.card: 51 Pegasi b, officially named Dimidium, is an extrasolar planet approximately 50 light-years away in the Pegasus constellation.
quotes.introduction: Dimidium was the first exoplanet to be discovered orbiting a main-sequence star, the Sun-like 51 Pegasi — a major astronomical discovery.
